transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Turn off the washing machine immediately and switch off the electricity at the mains. Do not touch any plugs or switches if they are wet or submerged in water to avoid electric shock. From what you have described, the most likely cause is detergent dispenser path — blocked/residue/oversudsing. Can you tell me whether water backs up out of the soap drawer or runs down the front from the dispenser DURING FILL?

I'm stood in socks on the wet floor right now, the water has run back towards the socket. The fuse box is in the hall and that floor is dry, so I'll go and switch it off. The water is coming from the front under the door though, not the soap drawer, that looks fine.

Good move switching off the mains - that is the safest thing to do given the water near the socket. Since the soap drawer looks fine and the water is coming from under the door, the most likely cause is a leak at the door seal (the rubber boot). Water can escape through a small tear or if something like a coin has pierced it. Another possibility is a split hose underneath the machine connecting to the pump. Please do not try to run the machine again until an engineer has checked it, especially with water near the electrical point.
ok the power's off at the fuse box now. the water is mostly still at the front under the door. should I check the door seal or just leave it till an engineer comes?

You have done the right thing by switching off the mains. Because water has reached the area around your plug and socket, this is an active electrical safety hazard. You must not attempt to dry it out, move the machine, or inspect internal components yourself until a qualified engineer has confirmed it is safe to do so. While we wait for them, you can safely wipe up standing water with towels to prevent further spread, but keep your hands and feet dry and stay away from the wet area near the socket. Do not try to pull the machine out if it risks disturbing the electrical connection or creating a slip hazard in that specific zone. The most likely cause of water coming from under the door is a leak through the rubber door seal (perhaps a tear or something caught in the folds) or a split hose inside the cabinet. However, because the water has compromised the electrical safety of your kitchen, this requires professional assessment and repair.
